text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: cont-batch streaming path p99 = 780ms (SLO 500ms) in us-west2. Auto-alerting threshold hit. Investigate; paging oncall.

jamie_oncall: on it. seeing p95 ~240ms but p99 spikes. rolling up dashboards now. any recent deploys to batcher?

aryan: no code deploys in last 2h. we did flip the batching config for a perf test ~30m ago (pack-shed disabled for a subset). could be related. metrics: cont-batcher queue depth increased ~3x.

lia_sre: logs show a bunch of hetero seqlen batches piling up, lot of padding amplification. streaming stalls align with large mixed-length bundles. grabbing flamegraphs.

devin_eng: can we temporarily reduce max_batch_size and re-enable pack-shed for cont-batcher? that should reduce amplification and favor streaming. I'm ready to push config.

jamie_oncall: +1 to config change. also let's route critical-tier traffic to non-continuous path (streaming fallback) for a short window. need a quick impact assessment before we change traffic routing.

tess_pm: customer telemetry — two paying customers (AcmeCorp, BrightApps) reported perceived slowdowns ~10:25-10:40. both are high-volume streaming users. queueing customers for notif if we change routing.

devin_eng: rolling config change now: decreasing cont-batcher max_batch_size from 256 -> 64, re-enable pack-shed, enable seqlen-aware binning. command:
```bash
# prod ops
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/cont-batcher BATCH_MAX_SIZE=64 PACK_SHED=1 SEQLEN_BINNING=1
```

support_bot: deploy-bot: Started rollout of cont-batcher config (deployment cont-batcher) by devin_eng at 10:33 UTC.

lia_sre: watching logs. early sign: number of large padding bundles decreased. KV cache evictions are a bit higher temporarily.

jamie_oncall: also applying routing change for critical-tier: policy -> prefer-streaming (non-cont-batch) for 15m window. hitting feature flag toggle: `route.policy.critical = prefer-streaming`.

devin_eng: routing toggled. command: `cfgctl set route.policy.critical prefer-streaming --env prod`

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation actions in flight (config and routing). Re-evaluating SLOs over next 5m.

lia_sre: metrics update @10:42: p95 = 220ms, p99 = 380ms (was 780ms). tail stalls dropping but still some outliers ~900ms on mixed seqlen.

jamie_oncall: good improvement. can we tune the batcher scheduling fairness to favor smaller seqlen requests next 30m? that should clear remaining tail.

aryan: scheduling tweak ready: set `fairness.window_ms=50` and `prefer_small_seq=1`. applying now.

devin_eng: tweak applied. logs show batching scheduler rebalanced; fewer large-blocking batches.

tess_pm: starting customer comms draft for AcmeCorp/BrightApps. recommending brief note: we identified transient latency spikes, mitigations applied, monitoring showing recovery.

support_bot: sent notification to AcmeCorp & BrightApps customer contacts (internal ticket IDs 6789, 6790).

lia_sre: final check @10:52: p95=200ms, p99=320ms. KV eviction rate stabilizing. no new customer reports in last 8 minutes.

jamie_oncall: handing off to next oncall (aryan) for monitoring for the next hour. we keep routing change for critical-tier for additional 10m then revert if stable. adding postmortem stub.

aryan: ack. I'll leave hooks for follow-ups: collect sample traces of remaining 900ms outliers and include in postmortem. noting root cause hypothesis: pack-shed disabled + perf test config created padding amplification under rush-hour mixed seqlen traffic -> tail latency.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> watching. Pager cleared.

jamie_oncall: :white_check_mark: summary: identified cont-batch packing/pading amplification during mixseq rush-hour; reverted test config, reduced max batch size, re-enabled pack-shed, adjusted scheduler fairness, routed critical traffic to fallback path temporarily. customers notified. follow-up: postmortem + tune default batch size under mixed-seqlen ramp tests.

aryan: filing postmortem doc and triage notes. closing thread unless new alerts. :eyes:
